top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001: Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) rewards a mature measurement advance. Demand estimation with endogenous prices and dynamic-industry models make substitution patterns, markups and welfare counterfactuals recoverable from market data. The core has about three decades of use in merger review and regulation, it has spread into trade, health and environmental economics, and its numerical and identification weaknesses have been studied. The BLP result has three authors, so the three-laureate cap does not split it. The main costs are toolkit versus discovery and the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. These do not outweigh the benefits of the award, and no award is a worse outcome than P001. My assessment of adoption and robustness rests on background knowledge and the committee's round-2 statements, not independent verification.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My co-authors (Kaplan, Axelson, Weisbach, Jenkinson, Lerner and others) are not credited on B001. I am an adjunct professor at Chicago Booth and a long-time committee overlap with Hassler and Krusell, who also support P001, is disclosed but not adjudicated.
